advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route `_ensure_blobs_present`'s top-up fetch through the same in-process + cross-process fetch locks that `_fetch_origin` uses (or otherwise serialize it per repo).
evidence: repo_snapshot.py:365 `with _fetch_lock_for(repo_root), _interprocess_lock(lock_path):` — _fetch_origin serializes fetch in- and cross-process
repo_snapshot.py:270-271 comment: 'In-process fetch coalescing: at most one fetch per repo at a time within this process (the cross-process flock handles the multi-process case).'
repo_snapshot.py:536-543 `_ensure_blobs_present` calls `subprocess.run(['git','-C',repo_root,*argv], ...)` with no fetch lock
cache.py:190 `with _sha_lock(sha):` — single-flight is per-SHA, so different SHAs materialize concurrently
advisory.finding: `_ensure_blobs_present` runs `git fetch --no-filter --refetch` via a bare `subprocess.run` without acquiring the in-process `_fetch_lock_for` or the cross-process `_interprocess_lock(fetch.lock)` that `_fetch_origin` deliberately holds. Since `cache.acquire` only single-flights per-SHA, two concurrent materializations of DIFFERENT SHAs on the same clone can now run overlapping, unsynchronized `--refetch` fetches (a heavy whole-object re-download) against the same object DB, defeating the documented fetch serialization.
scenarios: Two gates materialize two different attested SHAs of the same latched clone at once; both call _ensure_blobs_present and issue concurrent `git fetch --refetch`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide/comment on probe-failure semantics: on a probe timeout or error, either attempt the top-up anyway or fail closed, rather than silently skipping the batched fetch.
evidence: repo_snapshot.py:507-508 `if proc.returncode != 0: return False` (probe failure reads as 'nothing missing')
repo_snapshot.py:301-309 `_git` converts a TimeoutExpired into a CompletedProcess with returncode 124 and empty stdout
repo_snapshot.py:529 `if not _has_missing_blobs(...) or not _has_remote(...): return` — a False probe skips the top-up entirely
advisory.finding: When the offline probe `git rev-list ... --missing=print` times out, `_git` returns a synthetic returncode-124 CompletedProcess and `_has_missing_blobs` treats any non-zero returncode as 'nothing known to be missing' (returns False). A timed-out (or otherwise failed) probe therefore SKIPS the up-front batched top-up, and materialization silently degrades to git's per-blob lazy fetch — exactly the unbounded hours-long behaviour the ticket set out to eliminate.
scenarios: A very large tree whose rev-list probe legitimately exceeds _GIT_TIMEOUT, or a probe that errors for any reason, silently bypasses the batched fetch and falls back to per-blob lazy fetch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that injects subprocess.TimeoutExpired into _fetch_origin's subprocess.run and asserts a descriptive SnapshotFetchError is raised.
evidence: repo_snapshot.py:374-380: `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc: ... raise SnapshotFetchError(f"git fetch from '{remote}' timed out after {_GIT_TIMEOUT}s ...")`

ABSENCE: search of tests for `TimeoutExpired` and `SnapshotFetchError` shows the only SnapshotFetchError test (tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py:191) covers the auth/'could not read' returncode path, not a timeout; no test in test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py or elsewhere monkeypatches subprocess.run to raise TimeoutExpired for _fetch_origin.

The wrapper timeout test test_run_git_wrapper.py:61 verifies run_git PROPAGATES TimeoutExpired; _fetch_origin instead maps it to SnapshotFetchError via its own subprocess.run(timeout=...), a distinct contract left unverified.
advisory.finding: _fetch_origin's new timeout branch (maps subprocess.TimeoutExpired to a descriptive SnapshotFetchError, fail-closed) is untested — no test injects a fetch timeout to exercise it.
scenarios: A regression that drops the timeout= kwarg or the except branch would silently reintroduce a hang of the long-lived MCP server on a stuck remote, undetected by the suite.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch subprocess.run (as seen in test_store.py:169) to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired, call a resolve/materialize path that fetches, and assert pytest.raises(rs.SnapshotFetchError) with 'timed out' in the message.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that forces run_git to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired and asserts rs._git returns a CompletedProcess with returncode 124 and a descriptive stderr.
evidence: repo_snapshot.py:301-309: `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: return subprocess.CompletedProcess([...], 124, "", f"git timed out after {_GIT_TIMEOUT}s")`
_has_missing_blobs (repo_snapshot.py:507) does `if proc.returncode != 0: return False` — its behavior on a timed-out _git depends on this 124 mapping, yet no test drives _git through a timeout.
ABSENCE: no test in tests/ monkeypatches run_git/subprocess to raise TimeoutExpired against rs._git.
advisory.finding: _git's new TimeoutExpired handler (returns CompletedProcess with returncode 124) is untested; the probe and plumbing branch on returncode, so the fail-soft mapping is a load-bearing contract with no coverage.
scenarios: If the except branch were removed, a stuck git call under _git would raise instead of degrading to returncode 124, changing the probe/plumbing behavior — no test would catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: monkeypatch rs.run_git to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired, call rs._git(...), assert proc.returncode == 124 and 'timed out' in proc.stderr.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that captures git fetch argv for a fetch=True resolve/materialize and asserts --no-filter is used for the materialize-backing call while pure resolve_ref(...blobless default) uses --filter=blob:none.
evidence: repo_snapshot.py:356: `filter_arg = "--filter=blob:none" if blobless else "--no-filter"` and repo_snapshot.py:418/424 forward blobless to _fetch_origin — the primary fix mechanism.

test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py:129, 174, 199 all call materialize/materialize_tickets with `fetch=False`, so resolve_ref's `if has_remote:` fetch never runs and no test observes which filter arg is emitted; the one-RPC test (line 202) only counts `fetch` occurrences, not the filter flag.

ABSENCE: search of tests for `blobless` shows only the new fixture/test names; no test constructs a fetch=True resolution and asserts --no-filter (materialize-backing) vs --filter=blob:none (pure resolution).
advisory.finding: The core 'filter iff you will NOT materialize' policy — blobless=False -> --no-filter for materialize-backing resolutions vs --filter=blob:none for pure resolutions — is never asserted at the fetch-argument level; every materialize/materialize_tickets test passes fetch=False, bypassing resolve_ref/_fetch_origin entirely.
scenarios: A regression that reverts resolve_ref/_fetch_origin to always use --filter=blob:none (re-latching an ordinary clone into a promisor remote and re-introducing per-file lazy fetch) would pass the entire new suite, because _ensure_blobs_present masks the missing blobs and no test exercises the filtered-fetch path.
advisory.suggested_fix: Spy subprocess.run (as in test line 193) capturing fetch argv, run resolve_ref(sha, ..., blobless=False) against a real local remote and assert '--no-filter' in argv and '--filter=blob:none' not in argv; a paired case with the blobless default asserts the inverse.
